ownership_reason: Only the gold computes the whole part and the remainder of the division and decides how each is written (whole part and space only when the whole part is not zero, the remainder over the denominator); hops 2-4 pass the two ints, the three formats, the buffer and the alignment field along unchanged, and hop 1 only resets the alignment field and reads the numerator and the denominator of the fraction. The gold's javadoc promises the fraction in proper form, which "-1 -2 / 3" is not for -5/3. No change of the two ints above the gold restores it: the gold writes the denominator it receives, so it must stay 3, and no numerator n has n / 3 == -1 and n % 3 == 2 under truncating division; the size of the numerator drops the minus of the whole part. The convention is pinned outside the gold: the class javadoc of ProperFractionFormat and the javadoc of ProperFractionFormat.parse ('Minus signs are only allowed in the whole number part - i.e., "-3 1/2" is legitimate and denotes -7/2, but "-3 -1/2" is invalid'); ProperFractionFormat.parse rejects a negative numerator after the whole part ('minus signs should be leading') and rebuilds the value as (|w| * d + n) * MathUtils.sign(w), so the variant's text for -5/3 cannot be read back by the same format; FractionFormat.format (the improper form) writes the numerator with its sign when there is no whole part, as the gold does. Passing tests: FractionFormatTest testParseProperNegative ("-1 2 / 3" is -5/3), testParseProperInvalidMinus ("2 -2 / 3" is rejected) and testFormatNegative (through the chain: -1/2 is written "-1 / 2").
